proposals.relationship: Valverde explicitly places her work in Foucault’s tradition of developing theoretical tools through concrete historical research.
proposals.evidence_note: Own What Counts as Theory, Today? (2016), 174 and178, expressly identifies her Foucauldian working tradition and uses power/knowledge to explain how jurisdiction assigns different forms of governance. Her adoption of Bakhtin is explicitly an additional resource rather than abandonment of Foucault, while she rejects automatic eclecticism. This is a qualified intellectual debt stated in2016, not a first-publication date for her1991method or a claim that all her work derives from one thinker. Existing group route858 retains its broader moral-regulation context; original Foucault works are not newly read.
primary_locators: What Counts as Theory2016:174,178; full172–181 article

proposals.relationship: Valverde uses Derrida’s Spectres of Marx to challenge the opposition between theoretical sophistication and politically engaged labour history.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Deconstructive Marxism (1995),332–338, calls the book a resource for rethinking the theory/politics and ideal/material oppositions, while preserving Marx’s emancipatory project and the importance of historical inheritance. Her339–340 discussion explicitly stops short of Derrida’s undeconstructible justice and expresses reservations about its mystical context. The specific positive resource coexists with her earlier critique of Scott967; it is not a blanket endorsement, proof of personal contact or a new reading of Derrida’s original or Peggy Kamuf’s1994translation. Lorna Weir’s explicitly acknowledged help with deconstruction remains separate.
